data.why: app.py imports src.config/src.data/src.plots/src.science/src.transform and expects a data/demo_synthetic.csv fallback, but this commit (and the live GitHub repo) contains only app.py, README and docs at the root with no src/ or data/ directory at all, so the modules and demo fixture had to be authored from the exact API app.py calls and seeded into place before install; a second CSV with the same pscomppars-style schema is provided as a file to try through the sidebar uploader.

goals: Load the confirmed-planet composite table (via upload, since the live NASA TAP query has no network in this sandbox) and confirm it parses without a schema error
Compare stellar age versus planet radius, colouring by radius provenance, and read off the Spearman rank correlation with and without controlling for insolation
Compare orbital period versus planet radius, toggle the radius-valley line and Solar System reference points, and inspect the apparent gap in small-planet radii
Test how sample-quality filters (published-radius-only, uncertainty caps, controversial-flag exclusion) sharpen or wash out the radius-valley gap contrast in the dedicated valley tab
Run the young-versus-old host-star bootstrap comparison and check whether the confidence interval excludes a ratio of one, for all discovery methods and for transit-only
Export the filtered selection and the full cleaned table as CSV from the Table and export tab

review.summary: The tree tracks the app's main stages faithfully, and all nine screens I opened back up their nodes. But it leaves out the radius-valley test, one of the README's four main findings, and it reports bugs from code the setup agent wrote as if they were the tool's own. Fix by adding the valley phase, noting where the stand-in src/ came from, and tightening t2, t8 and t9 and the goal's wording before filing.
